errors.retryDescription: For 429 and transient 5xx errors, use exponential backoff with jitter (for example, a random delay of 100–1,500 ms that doubles on each retry). Include an Idempotency-Key header on write operations to avoid duplicates.
errors.helpDescription: If you consistently see 4xx errors, something in the request likely needs adjusting. If you see 5xx errors, the issue may be with our services or an upstream provider. We include clear messages and a generation_id to help you diagnose the problem quickly.

errors.notFoundWhen: The requested model or resource could not be found.
errors.notFoundAction: Check the ID and confirm the resource is available to your account.
errors.rateLimitWhen: You have sent requests too quickly or reached a usage limit.
errors.rateLimitAction: Wait, then retry with exponential backoff; check your rate limits.
errors.serverWhen: An unexpected error occurred in our service.
errors.serverAction: Retry after a short delay. Contact support if it continues.
errors.badGatewayWhen: An upstream provider returned an invalid response.
errors.badGatewayAction: Retry after a short delay; check the provider status if it continues.
errors.unavailableWhen: The service or upstream provider is temporarily unavailable.
errors.unavailableAction: Retry after a short delay with exponential backoff.
errors.timeoutWhen: Our service did not receive a timely response from an upstream provider.
errors.timeoutAction: Retry after a short delay, preferably with a different provider.
errors.bucketsDescription: Two simple buckets: 4xx errors mean your request needs attention; 5xx errors point to our service or an upstream provider. We return descriptive messages to help you resolve issues quickly.
